summary: Survey 2025-2026 agent-orchestration strategies, map them against the StarlingAI swarm, and rank verified integration wins
logs: research angles done: 6/6, capability maps: 2/2, total patterns: 47
synthesis produced 8 recommendations; verifying top 6 against the repo

confirmed.title: B37 lean tool catalog: search_tools/load_tool progressive disclosure instead of ~80 always-loaded schemas
confirmed.basedOn: Anthropic Tool Search Tool / progressive tool disclosure (~85% token reduction, tool-selection accuracy 49%->74% on large catalogs)
confirmed.ourGap: The improvement roadmap's own 'biggest product-wide token lever' is explicitly unimplemented: all ~80 full tool schemas ride every orchestrator iteration, on top of the 24.7K prompt monolith (25-28s prefill per call on local models). Prompt trimming exists but never touches the tool catalog.
confirmed.integrationSketch: Keep a small pinned core set per agent (delegation, record_plan, recall_context, share_finding, write/read); register everything else as name+one-line summary only. Add a search_tools meta-tool backed by the EXISTING pgvector embeddings + Qwen reranker sidecar (packages/core/src/db/vector-store.ts, retrieval/reranker.ts) and a load_tool that injects the full schema for the rest of the session (append-only, so KV-cache safe). Enforce TOOL_TIER_MAP at load time in guardrails/tool-tiers.ts. Touch: tool registry, agent/turn-system-prompt.ts (assembleTurnSystemMessages catalog section), config/schemas/orchestration.ts flag leanToolCatalog (default-off). Test: unit tests that tier gating survives lazy load and that pinned set is stable; measure promptChars/llmTimeMs via existing turn-metrics phaseTimingsMs; gate on the user's pass^k shard (routing-sensitive cases) before default-on.
confirmed.risks: Model may fail to search for a tool it doesn't know exists (mitigate: category index line per tool family, and sub-agents keep their small explicit tool lists — only the orchestrator goes lazy). Routing/eval regressions possible; strictly pass^k-gated.
confirmed.verifyNotes: Verdict: real gap, but the claim overstates baseline cost and the sketch under-credits existing infra. (1) Claim correction: "~80 full schemas ride every orchestrator iteration" is true only in toolMode=hybrid; the shipped default is orchestration_only (~17 always-available + ~13 orchestration = ~30 full schemas per iteration, runtime.ts:1243). Sub-agents separately carry their full configured schema sets (sub-agent.ts:1895), reranked but never pruned except under E19 storm degradation. (2) Sketch modules all exist: tools/registry.ts, agent/turn-system-prompt.ts (assembleTurnSystemMessages:88), config/schemas/orchestration.ts, guardrails/tool-tiers.ts (TOOL_TIER_MAP:29, execute-time enforcement so tier gating survives lazy load), db/vector-store.ts, retrieval/reranker.ts. (3) Seam corrections: tool schemas travel in the LLM tools param (runtime.ts:1243 / sub-agent.ts:1895), NOT in assembleTurnSystemMessages — only the name+one-line summary section belongs in the prompt (precedent: buildSubAgentToolInventory in agent/sub-agent-prompt-guidance.ts:75); search_tools should reuse the existing in-memory tool-embedding path (searchToolsByEmbedding + warmToolEmbeddings), not pgvector vector-store.ts / reranker sidecar as the sketch says — that would be redundant re-plumbing. (4) Design landmines already documented in the repo's own roadmap: §F line 140 warns pruning tools out of allowedToolNameSet makes a named-but-dropped call hit the hard not_in_turn block (runtime.ts:3221) — load_tool must extend the allowed set, and §E line 120 requires tier checks stay strict. (5) The sketch's "append-only, so KV-cache safe" claim is dubious: local chat templates (LM Studio/Qwen) serialize tool schemas into the prompt prefix, so injecting a schema into the tools param mid-session invalidates the prefill cache; an appended system-message schema injection would be cache-safe but needs the not_in_turn allowlist extended in tandem. Flag-gated default-off + pass^k gating matches repo practice and the roadmap's own B37 entry.

confirmed.title: Code Mode: one sandboxed run_tool_script tool over a generated typed client of the tool registry
confirmed.basedOn: Anthropic code-execution-with-MCP / Programmatic Tool Calling (-98.7% tokens on chained tasks, ~38% billed-input reduction on 75-tool agents) + Cloudflare Code Mode
confirmed.ourGap: Every multi-step flow (research->filter->write, mail sequences) costs one LLM round-trip per tool call, and intermediate data round-trips through the model's context. Nothing in the swarm lets an agent chain tools in deterministic code; the docker sandbox infra exists but only for self-dev code, not registry-backed tool scripting.
confirmed.integrationSketch: Codegen a typed TS client from the existing tool registry (schemas are already zod/JSONSchema) laid out as files; new run_tool_script tool executes model-written scripts in the existing container-runner.ts sandbox with a host-side broker that proxies each client call back through the real tool pipeline — so TOOL_TIER_MAP approval gates, guardrails, per-tool caps, and audit events still fire per underlying call (critical: the sandbox never gets raw credentials, matching the auth-proxy pattern). Grant initially to coder-class agents + orchestrator at high/max effort only. Flag codeModeToolScripting default-off. Test: unit tests for codegen fidelity + broker tier enforcement (a script calling a Tier-2 tool must still hit the approval gate); pass^k shard with 2-3 chained-flow cases comparing tool-iteration counts and tokens (turn_scorecard toolIterations) vs baseline.
confirmed.risks: Largest security surface of the eight — mitigated by broker-side enforcement (tiers/caps/redaction run on the host, not in the sandbox). Weak local models may write buggy scripts; bound retries at 2 and fall back to classic per-call tool use. Land incrementally: broker + codegen + read-only tools first.
confirmed.verifyNotes: Verdict: real gap, but the CLAIMED GAP is materially overstated and must be rewritten. run_tool_pipeline already ships (default-on, granted to data_analyst) and collapses multi-tool chains into ONE LLM round-trip with {{steps.<id>.output}} piping between steps, per-step tier/approval/audit via executeTool, agent-allowlist scoping, and delegation-tool blocking — its header comment states this exact round-trip motivation. What is genuinely missing is only the code-mode delta: (1) arbitrary deterministic logic (loops/branches/filter-transform — the 'filter' in research->filter->write cannot be expressed today; templating is whole-output string substitution, and all step outputs still return to the model concatenated at the end), (2) a generated typed client (no codegen exists anywhere), (3) a sandbox->host broker (none exists: container-entrypoint.ts runs executeTool IN-process inside the container; tool-sandbox-runner.ts runs code with zero tool access). Sketch: named modules are real — agent/container-runner.ts, guardrails/tool-tiers.ts TOOL_TIER_MAP, JSON-Schema tool params (registry.ts:14), toolIterations metric (agent/turn-metrics.ts) — and the brokered-executeTool seam is proven plausible by run_tool_pipeline. Three corrections: (a) container-runner.ts is a sub-agent runner (docker run agent-worker, stdin JSON payload, heartbeat watchdog), not a script executor — code mode needs a new entrypoint mode or should build on tool-sandbox-runner's runInSandbox, and the broker RPC channel is net-new either way; (b) there is NO existing 'auth-proxy pattern' in the repo — container-runner currently passes providerApiKey INTO the container (ContainerTaskPayload), so credential isolation must be built, not 'matched'; (c) the broker MUST enforce the per-agent allowlist and BLOCKED_STEP_TOOLS itself, because executeTool checks tier only — tool-pipeline.ts documents and solves this exact pitfall (lines 57-60, 150-152) and is the reference implementation for broker semantics. Any implementation should be framed as extending run_tool_pipeline's guarantees to scripted control flow, and the pass^k comparison baseline should be run_tool_pipeline, not raw per-call round-trips.

confirmed.title: Durable task-graph execution: persist node results, resume-on-timeout instead of honesty backstop
confirmed.basedOn: LangGraph super-step checkpointing / DBOS state-in-Postgres durable execution (60%+ wasted re-processing cut); complements the just-shipped excludeDelegationWaitFromTurnBudget from the other side of the e3cf6c22 failure class
confirmed.ourGap: Workflow JOBS checkpoint completed steps (jobs.ts saveWorkflowCheckpoint), but run_task_graph node results are in-memory only: a turn that hits the budget ceiling mid-graph loses all completed nodes and arms the honesty backstop / incomplete-caveat stamp. Stage 9 checkpoints are sub-agent-level, gateway-HTTP-resume only, 24h TTL, truncated — there is no orchestrator-facing 'resume this graph' path.
confirmed.integrationSketch: Persist each completed node's distilled result + artifact refs to Postgres keyed (sessionId, turnId, graphHash, nodeId) inside run_task_graph's node-completion path (tools/sub-agent.ts:2748-2840), reusing the jobs.ts jsonb round-trip pattern. On timeout/abort, turn-finalize-guards.ts records a resumable-graph marker in the session slot next to the TurnPlan; the next user turn (or a new resume_task_graph tool granted to the orchestrator) re-invokes the graph with completed nodes skipped (same shape as blockFailedDependents but inverted). Flag durableTaskGraph default-off. Test: unit tests for skip-completed semantics + graphHash invalidation when the task text changes; an agent-eval case with an artificially low turn budget asserting the second turn finishes without re-running node 1 (expectArtifact + toolIterations delta).
confirmed.risks: Stale-resume hazard: world state may have changed between turns — TTL the records (hours) and hash the node task text so edits invalidate. Must not double-fire side-effectful nodes (write/send); mark nodes idempotent-or-not at validation time and never auto-skip non-idempotent ones.
confirmed.verifyNotes: CONFIRMED GAP with one overstatement. (1) run_task_graph (packages/core/src/tools/sub-agent.ts:2748-2958) keeps completed/failed/blocked node state in local Sets, graphId is timestamp-based, and there is no resume_task_graph tool or durableTaskGraph flag anywhere (grep: 0 hits). (2) Stage 9 checkpoints (packages/core/src/swarm/checkpoints.ts) are exactly as claimed — sub-agent-level, truncated (2KB/4KB/8KB), 24h TTL, resume only via gateway HTTP route (gateway/index.ts:5176) — and are actually DEAD SCAFFOLDING: createCheckpoint/pauseCheckpoint have zero production callers (tests only), so nothing ever checkpoints during real runs; also stored on disk + in-process Map, not Redis as its doc comment claims. (3) jobs.ts prior art confirmed: saveWorkflowCheckpoint at agent/jobs.ts:210 with Postgres jsonb round-trip (B31, lines 969-970). OVERSTATEMENT: 'loses all completed nodes' is too strong — each completed node's delegation already persists distilled session-scoped evidence via tools/sub-agent.ts:2346-2355 (appendPartialResult 1200-char summary + artifact refs, writeSharedFact, both Redis 4h TTL, plus graphPromoteFact to the durable graph), and interrupted-delegation-evidence.ts/evidence-recovery.ts salvage partial evidence into the same-turn caveated synthesis. What is genuinely missing is the RESUME substance: graph/node-keyed persistence, skip-completed re-invocation, resumable-graph marker. The implementation should reuse that existing shared-facts persistence rather than duplicate it. SKETCH: all named modules real — tools/sub-agent.ts node-completion path (completed.add actually at ~2911, just past the quoted 2748-2840 range; blockFailedDependents to invert at 2828), turn-finalize-guards.ts (real terminal-guard module running honesty backstops/incomplete caveats — plausible marker site), TurnPlan per-session slot pattern real (agent/turn-plan.ts persistTurnPlan → swarm/memory.ts writeTurnPlan, Redis 4h TTL — a resumable-graph marker there inherits 4h TTL, acceptable for next-turn resume), jobs.ts jsonb pattern reusable though a (sessionId,turnId,graphHash,nodeId) keyed store is net-new schema (jobs stores checkpoints on the job payload row) and graphHash is net-new (trivial). Flag default-off in config/schemas/orchestration.ts matches repo convention and the memory-noted pass^k eval gate.

confirmed.title: Tool-equipped, clean-context QA verifier + no-PASS-without-evidence invariant
confirmed.basedOn: Agent-as-a-Judge (transcript-only judges catch ~1 in 5 real defects) + Cognition zero-shared-context reviewer (58% of severe issues, findings routed back to the builder) + externally-grounded Reflexion (self-critique without an oracle doesn't work)
confirmed.ourGap: qaDeliveryLoop/riskGatedQA judge the TRANSCRIPT and fail OPEN (parseQaVerdict treats unparseable verdicts as PASS) — a confident narration passes; the verifier also inherits session context, so it inherits the builder's blind spots. No rule forces a verdict to be backed by a deterministic artifact.
confirmed.integrationSketch: Three composable pieces on existing seams: (1) run the QA verdict as a runSubAgent with a CLEAN context (artifact paths + acceptanceCriteria from the TurnPlan only, no shared facts / builder transcript) — sub-agent.ts already supports fresh history + restricted tool lists; (2) grant it read_file/verify_app/HTTP-probe tools so it opens the artifact or runs the served app instead of rating prose (verify_app already exists from the harness wave); (3) extend parseQaVerdict in qa-delivery-loop.ts: a PASS must carry an evidence field (test output, probe result, file stat) or it is downgraded to UNVERIFIED, which routes into the existing prependTurnIncompleteCaveat-style stamp rather than blocking delivery (preserves fail-open shipping while killing rubber-stamps). Findings return to the ORIGINAL builder for the fix round (current escalate() path), never to the reviewer. Flag qaToolJudge default-off. Test: unit tests for the evidence-required verdict parse; eval cases with a planted defect (truncated HTML app, wrong-port server) that a transcript judge passes and a tool judge must catch.
confirmed.risks: Adds one sub-agent run + tool calls to QA'd turns (bounded: only riskGated/high-effort turns, cheap routing-tier model). Clean context can make the reviewer miss intent nuances — acceptanceCriteria quality becomes load-bearing, which pressures record_plan quality (acceptable: planFirst is default-on).
confirmed.verifyNotes: GAP CONFIRMED. (1) parseQaVerdict fails open exactly as claimed: packages/core/src/agent/qa-delivery-loop.ts:32-40 — any text without "FAIL" (including empty/unparseable) returns {pass:true}, deliberately documented. (2) Both delivery-gate QA arms are prose-only model calls with zero tools: qaDeliveryLoop check() at packages/core/src/agent/runtime.ts:4369-4393 (bare 2-message verdict call over answer text + criteria), riskGatedQA verify at packages/core/src/agent/turn-finalize-guards.ts:410-431 (forceSynthesis = the SAME model with the FULL builder transcript self-verifying — the "inherits builder's blind spots" claim is accurate for THIS arm). (3) No evidence-required-PASS invariant exists anywhere; QaVerdict has no evidence field; flag qaToolJudge does not exist. PARTIAL PRIOR ART that does NOT close the gap: reviewed_deliverable scene (workspace/scenes/10-core-scenes.jsonc:163) has a tool-equipped reviewer panel (source_verifier: web_fetch/read_file/url_inspect; quality_supervisor) but is opt-in scene routing during BUILD, not the final delivery gate, with no verdict-evidence rule; verify_app (packages/core/src/tools/serve-app.ts:442) is a real deterministic artifact verifier with pass/fail + audit logging but is only granted to builder agents, never wired into a QA verdict. SKETCH SEAMS ALL REAL: sub-agent.ts documents "Fresh conversation history (no access to parent session)" (line 8; history built fresh at line 1984) with per-agent restricted tool lists (allowedTools line 1929, inlineConfig line 1477); prependTurnIncompleteCaveat exists (packages/core/src/agent/citation-honesty.ts:81, already used on both timeout early-returns in runtime.ts:1613/1779); escalate() exists (turn-finalize-guards.ts:456-494, qaDeliveryLoopEscalateToCoordinator → delegate_to_agent mission_coordinator, which re-plans and re-delegates to builders — matches the sketch's "back to the builder, never the reviewer" intent); parseQaVerdict is a pure unit-tested function (qa-delivery-loop.test.ts) — clean extension point; TurnPlan.acceptanceCriteria exists (turn-plan.ts:37). TWO INACCURACIES TO CORRECT IN THE CLAIM/SKETCH: (a) the qaDeliveryLoop check is ALREADY clean-context — it sees ONLY the answer + criteria, no transcript/shared facts — so its defect is blindness (cannot verify against any artifact/evidence even in principle), not inherited context; the context-inheritance critique applies only to the riskGatedQA forceSynthesis arm. (b) TurnPlan carries NO artifact paths — the verifier's artifact inputs must come from turn tool-call records / workspace-write tracking (the claimsArtifactWrittenButUnproduced machinery proves this tracking exists), not from the plan object. Also note the fail-open design is intentional and pervasive ("the gate never blocks delivery" invariant, docs at qa-delivery-loop.ts:5-16), so the sketch's downgrade-to-UNVERIFIED-caveat rather than block is the correct integration shape and consistent with the repo's honesty-stamp pattern (v0.40.1 prependTurnIncompleteCaveat precedent). Default-off flag + pass^k eval requirement matches repo convention for tuned-prompt/gate changes.

confirmed.title: Progress ledger: per-iteration structural progress check + stall-counter forced replan + plan recitation
confirmed.basedOn: Magentic-One dual-ledger orchestration (GA in Microsoft Agent Framework 1.0) + Manus todo.md recitation against lost-in-the-middle drift
confirmed.ourGap: record_plan captures the Task Ledger half only. Nothing tracks per-iteration progress against the plan mid-turn: stall handling is either sub-agent-level (progress-verifier) or terminal (turn-oversight forced delivery, dead-end-break), so a coordinator that keeps re-delegating a doomed step burns the budget with no escalate-to-REPLAN path; and on long turns the turn-0 plan gets buried/compacted out of the model's attention.
confirmed.integrationSketch: In the runtime loop (agent/turn-tool-execution.ts post-processing or turn-prepare.ts per-iteration hook): maintain a structural per-step ledger on the existing TurnPlan slot (turn-plan.ts) — step status derived from delegation outcomes/artifacts (language-free signals: new artifact, share_finding count, delegation success), plus a consecutive-no-progress counter. On N (default 2) no-progress iterations against the same step, inject a single bounded directive forcing a record_plan REVISION (mark step blocked, choose alternative) instead of another delegation — reusing the turn-corrective.ts bounded-directive machinery. Recitation: every K iterations append a 3-line plan-state message (done/pending/blocked) at the context tail — append-only, so KV-cache safe, and droppable under budget pressure. Flag progressLedger default-off. Test: unit tests for status derivation + stall counter; eval case with an intentionally impossible research step asserting a plan revision fires before iteration exhaustion (audit event plan_revision_forced).
confirmed.risks: Over-eager replanning can thrash on slow-but-progressing steps — the no-progress signal must count delegation-in-flight as progress (delegation-wait exclusion already gives the timing hook). Adds a small recurring context cost (bounded 3 lines).
confirmed.verifyNotes: REAL GAP, but with substantial partial overlap the implementation MUST extend rather than duplicate. What exists: (1) turn-oversight.ts + runtime.ts:1670-1795 already implements a turn-level structural progress check (classifyTurnProgress over tokens/toolCalls/delegations/artifacts/delegationFailures), churn detection, a bounded LLM judge, ONE corrective redirect directive, then a forced-delivery floor — but it is max-effort ONLY (line 1679), behind maxEffortTurnOversight default-OFF (orchestration.ts:276), sampled on a 180s wall-clock window (not per-iteration), not plan-step-aware, and its 're-plan' is a free-form directive, not a forced record_plan revision. (2) runtime.ts:3807-3845 (D16) is an all-tier consecutive-delegation-FAILURE counter: 1 failure → '[DELEGATION FAILED] try a different strategy' nudge; ≥2 → TERMINAL forced synthesis — it resets on any successful delegation (a succeeding-but-no-plan-progress loop is invisible) and escalates terminally, never to a plan revision. (3) progress-verifier.ts is sub-agent-level max-effort, exactly as claimed. (4) turn-plan.ts TurnPlanStep has NO status field; no ledger, no stall counter, no plan_revision_forced audit event, no recitation; plan is read only at finalization QA (turn-finalize-guards.ts:358,447), by sub-agents (sub-agent.ts:2105), and by max-effort oversight; compaction (session.ts:609-613) pins only the first user message, so the buried-plan claim holds. So the recommendation's three concrete pieces — per-step ledger on TurnPlan, all-tier per-iteration same-step stall counter escalating to a forced plan REVISION (non-terminal), and periodic plan-state recitation — do not exist. The claimed-gap characterization is accurate modulo one nuance: max-effort oversight DOES have a non-terminal redirect middle step, but it is one-shot, default-off, and max-only. SKETCH: sound with two naming corrections — turn-prepare.ts is PRE-loop setup only (not a per-iteration hook; the real seam is runtime.ts's main loop where D16/steering/oversight already inject bounded messages, plus the turn-tool-execution.ts post-processing seam), and turn-corrective.ts is specifically the final-QA corrective build/reroute delegations, not generic bounded-directive machinery (the reusable patterns are turn-oversight.ts's TurnProgressSample machinery and the inline [OVERSIGHT]/[DELEGATION FAILED] injections). Recommend implementing by generalizing turn-oversight.ts's structural sampler to all tiers + per-iteration cadence + plan-step attribution, reusing _consecutiveDelegationFailures/_iterationToolSets/_turnDelegationCount counters already threaded in runtime.ts, and adding the audit event to audit/schema.ts (precedent: turn_oversight_redirected). Default-off flag matches repo pass^k convention.

allRecommendations.title: KV-cache-stable prompt layout + tool-result-clearing compaction tier
allRecommendations.basedOn: Manus KV-cache-aware context rules (stable prefix, append-only, never reorder tools) + Anthropic server-side tool-result clearing (+29% agentic evals, 84% token cut on long workflows)
allRecommendations.ourGap: assembleTurnSystemMessages re-runs a priority-ordered budget trimmer with re-measure loop EVERY iteration, and dynamic sections (routing hints, capability capsules, recalled memory) sit in the system prompt — churning the prefix and killing both LM Studio prefix-cache and Anthropic prompt-cache; with ~100:1 input:output ratios this is the dominant unaddressed latency cost. History compaction jumps straight from raw history to pin+digest with no light-touch middle tier that nulls stale tool-result bodies while keeping the calls visible.
allRecommendations.integrationSketch: (1) Audit + freeze: make system prompt and tool-catalog bytes deterministic per session (stable JSON key order, no timestamps up top) in agent/turn-system-prompt.ts; relocate all per-iteration dynamic content ([CAPABILITY CANDIDATES] from discovery-prefetch.ts, plan state, effort addendum) to appended messages at the context tail. Add cache_control breakpoints in providers/AnthropicProvider after the stable blocks. (2) New compaction stage in agent/session.ts BEFORE digestHistoryMessage: replace tool-result bodies older than N iterations with a one-line digest + placeholder, threshold wired to the effort tier via effort-context.ts. Emit a prompt_prefix_invalidated audit event when the assembled prefix differs from the previous iteration to make regressions visible. Test: unit test byte-stability of two consecutive assemblies for a fixed session; A/B llmTimeMs via phaseTimingsMs (A1) on a long research turn against the local stack; flag toolResultClearing default-off, pass^k-gated.
allRecommendations.risks: Clearing a tool result the model later needs forces a re-fetch (keep the call + digest line so it knows what it did and can re-run). Moving sections to the tail changes prompt semantics — needs eval. Prefix-stability work can conflict with the existing budget trimmer; trimmer must become monotonic (only append/trim at tail).

Must not double-fire side-effectful nodes (write/send); mark nodes idempotent-or-not at validation time and never auto-skip non-idempotent ones.

allRecommendations.title: Tool-equipped, clean-context QA verifier + no-PASS-without-evidence invariant
allRecommendations.basedOn: Agent-as-a-Judge (transcript-only judges catch ~1 in 5 real defects) + Cognition zero-shared-context reviewer (58% of severe issues, findings routed back to the builder) + externally-grounded Reflexion (self-critique without an oracle doesn't work)
allRecommendations.ourGap: qaDeliveryLoop/riskGatedQA judge the TRANSCRIPT and fail OPEN (parseQaVerdict treats unparseable verdicts as PASS) — a confident narration passes; the verifier also inherits session context, so it inherits the builder's blind spots. No rule forces a verdict to be backed by a deterministic artifact.
allRecommendations.integrationSketch: Three composable pieces on existing seams: (1) run the QA verdict as a runSubAgent with a CLEAN context (artifact paths + acceptanceCriteria from the TurnPlan only, no shared facts / builder transcript) — sub-agent.ts already supports fresh history + restricted tool lists; (2) grant it read_file/verify_app/HTTP-probe tools so it opens the artifact or runs the served app instead of rating prose (verify_app already exists from the harness wave); (3) extend parseQaVerdict in qa-delivery-loop.ts: a PASS must carry an evidence field (test output, probe result, file stat) or it is downgraded to UNVERIFIED, which routes into the existing prependTurnIncompleteCaveat-style stamp rather than blocking delivery (preserves fail-open shipping while killing rubber-stamps). Findings return to the ORIGINAL builder for the fix round (current escalate() path), never to the reviewer. Flag qaToolJudge default-off. Test: unit tests for the evidence-required verdict parse; eval cases with a planted defect (truncated HTML app, wrong-port server) that a transcript judge passes and a tool judge must catch.
allRecommendations.risks: Adds one sub-agent run + tool calls to QA'd turns (bounded: only riskGated/high-effort turns, cheap routing-tier model). Clean context can make the reviewer miss intent nuances — acceptanceCriteria quality becomes load-bearing, which pressures record_plan quality (acceptable: planFirst is default-on).

allRecommendations.title: Progress ledger: per-iteration structural progress check + stall-counter forced replan + plan recitation
allRecommendations.basedOn: Magentic-One dual-ledger orchestration (GA in Microsoft Agent Framework 1.0) + Manus todo.md recitation against lost-in-the-middle drift
allRecommendations.ourGap: record_plan captures the Task Ledger half only. Nothing tracks per-iteration progress against the plan mid-turn: stall handling is either sub-agent-level (progress-verifier) or terminal (turn-oversight forced delivery, dead-end-break), so a coordinator that keeps re-delegating a doomed step burns the budget with no escalate-to-REPLAN path; and on long turns the turn-0 plan gets buried/compacted out of the model's attention.
allRecommendations.integrationSketch: In the runtime loop (agent/turn-tool-execution.ts post-processing or turn-prepare.ts per-iteration hook): maintain a structural per-step ledger on the existing TurnPlan slot (turn-plan.ts) — step status derived from delegation outcomes/artifacts (language-free signals: new artifact, share_finding count, delegation success), plus a consecutive-no-progress counter. On N (default 2) no-progress iterations against the same step, inject a single bounded directive forcing a record_plan REVISION (mark step blocked, choose alternative) instead of another delegation — reusing the turn-corrective.ts bounded-directive machinery. Recitation: every K iterations append a 3-line plan-state message (done/pending/blocked) at the context tail — append-only, so KV-cache safe, and droppable under budget pressure. Flag progressLedger default-off. Test: unit tests for status derivation + stall counter; eval case with an intentionally impossible research step asserting a plan revision fires before iteration exhaustion (audit event plan_revision_forced).
allRecommendations.risks: Over-eager replanning can thrash on slow-but-progressing steps — the no-progress signal must count delegation-in-flight as progress (delegation-wait exclusion already gives the timing hook). Adds a small recurring context cost (bounded 3 lines).

allRecommendations.title: Guard-triggered local-to-Anthropic escalation retry (structural cascade, never self-assessed)
allRecommendations.basedOn: RouteLLM/UCCI calibrated cascades + Cognition's finding that weak models cannot self-detect the need to escalate — escalation must come from an external signal
allRecommendations.ourGap: Provider mixing is static per-agent config; when a local-model delegation fails a guard (evidence anchoring, failed-research backstop, QA reject, disagreement, stall counter), the swarm's only moves are caveat-and-ship or bounded same-model retry. There is no path that re-runs the failed SUBTASK once on the stronger provider — the cheapest quality lever the two-provider setup leaves on the table.
allRecommendations.integrationSketch: A small escalation broker: when a designated guard fires on a delegated result (hooks already exist in turn-finalize-guards.ts / qa-delivery-loop.ts escalate() / the new stall counter), re-issue that ONE delegation with a provider override to the claude preset via the existing mergeAgentModelOverride/applyActiveModelPreset plumbing (providers/index.ts, sub-agent-model-config.ts), max 1 escalation per turn, cost-governance-checked against the existing budget thresholds before firing. Log an escalation outcome record in agent/outcomes.ts so over time the trigger set is tuned on data (which guard trips actually flip to success). Flag escalateOnGuardTrip default-off; escalation NEVER prompted to the local model itself. Test: unit test the broker (guard event -> single override retry -> no recursion); eval shard comparing pass^k and cost with the flag on vs off for research cases where local models fail evidence anchoring.
allRecommendations.risks: Cost leak if guards are noisy (bounded: 1/turn + cost-governance gate + default-off). Requires ANTHROPIC key configured — must degrade to current behavior silently when absent. Guard-trip set is the calibration surface; start with the two highest-precision guards only.

allRecommendations.title: Local groundedness-scorer sidecar (HHEM-2.1-Open class) as a tier-2 faithfulness rail on RAG-grounded answers
allRecommendations.basedOn: Vectara HHEM-2.x / Patronus Lynx small NLI faithfulness models + the tiered verification stack (deterministic -> small scorer -> sampled frontier judge)
allRecommendations.ourGap: Evidence anchoring is lexical token-overlap (named weakness: a fluent wrong answer that reuses evidence vocabulary passes), and the doc-grounding honesty exclusion only verifies retrieval HAPPENED, not that the answer is faithful to the retrieved chunks. There is no semantic groundedness check anywhere, and no tier-2 layer between the structural guards and the (fail-open) LLM QA verdicts.
allRecommendations.integrationSketch: New CPU/GPU sidecar container following the exact docker/reranker-qwen precedent (compose service + TOOL_TIER_MAP-free internal HTTP client in packages/core/src/retrieval/) serving an NLI faithfulness model; a scoreGroundedness(evidenceChunks, answer) client called from turn-finalize-guards.ts on answers whose evidence came from engram/pgvector retrieval or shared findings. Per-effort thresholds: low = warn + reuse the existing unverified-caveat stamp; high/max = one bounded re-synthesis with more retrieval (existing corrective-build machinery). Errors are uncorrelated with the generator by construction — different architecture/lineage. Flag groundednessRail default-off; sidecar optional in compose (degrades to no-op, with a health-check line in /api/health/subsystems so silent-degradation is visible, unlike engram today). Test: golden (evidence, faithful/unfaithful answer) pairs as an integration test against the sidecar; eval on document-RAG cases with planted contradictions; latency budget assertion (<1s) via phaseTimingsMs.
allRecommendations.risks: 4k-token context limit on HHEM-class models forces chunked scoring with min-aggregation; false positives on legitimately synthesized (multi-hop) answers — start warn-only. Another sidecar to operate on a single-GPU box (CPU inference is acceptable for this model size). Must not fire on non-RAG answers (scope strictly to retrieval-grounded turns).

capabilityWeaknesses: routing-intent subsystem rated 'needs-attention' in the June 2026 audit: softRoutingEnforcement misses the dominant prompt (B34), two divergent artifact-intent classifiers drift (B35), and ~6 bilingual-keyword detector bags remain pending structural de-lex (B42.2, explicitly 'do LAST, one intent at a time') — docs/improvement-roadmap-2026-06.md:24,103-107

The de-lexicalization hardwired sourceSensitive/freshnessSensitive classifiers to false (intent-classifier.ts:260-261 per docs/honesty-restoration-2026-07.md), silently killing many honesty guards; they were restored structurally but most remain default-OFF pending the user's pass^k eval (only enabled in the deployment shard config/gateway/40-orchestration.jsonc, not schema defaults)

deliverable-intent.ts builder-election de-lex is explicitly DEFERRED (entangled with live honesty guards, pass^k-gated) — per project memory; the module still carries keyword-shaped deliverable classifiers

Orchestrator monolith prompt ~24.7K tokens re-sent every iteration (25-28s prefill/call on slow local models); staged decomposition is partial — S1/S3/S4 landed but default-off in schema, S2 (lean planning prompt) was disproven — docs/staged-orchestration.md

~80 full tool schemas re-sent to the orchestrator every iteration (B37 lean tool-catalog identified as 'biggest product-wide token lever', not yet implemented) — docs/improvement-roadmap-2026-06.md:18,106

Per-stage turn timings unmeasured (A1 phaseTimingsMs is the 'meta-unblocker'), iteration-0 memory/skill/prefetch retrievals run serially (A7), and staged stages are not effort-relaxable (A9) — docs/improvement-roadmap-2026-06.md:15,61,66,95

Outcome-weighted routing is inert until 25 similar-class samples exist and its task-class fingerprint is a crude top-3-keyword Jaccard (agent/outcomes.ts:269-283) — cold-start agents get no outcome signal

Keyword routing scores 'rarely cross 0.72 even for unambiguous specialist matches' due to aggressive normalization, so the keyword-only floor had to be dropped to 0.45 (comment in tools/agent-routing.ts:25-35) — routing quality degrades notably when the embedding endpoint is down

mission_coordinator's system prompt hardcodes deployment-specific tuning ('AT MOST 2 parallel tasks', 'single local GPU', 5-min-per-researcher wall-clock math) into the workspace agent shard — brittle on other hardware (workspace/agents/10-core-agents.jsonc:20)

max effort deliberately turns QA gates and the never-empty watchdog OFF, and its rescue (maxEffortTurnOversight) plus the semantic progress judge (progressVerifierSemantic) are both default-off pending live eval — a stuck max-effort turn currently relies only on the structural stall guard (config/schemas/orchestration.ts:264-276,376-384)

Stage 9 task checkpoints are resumed only via gateway HTTP endpoints (gateway/index.ts:78) — no orchestrator-facing resume tool; checkpoints expire after 24h TTL and content is truncated (8KB conversation summary / 4KB progress note)

Ephemeral agents judged under-used and the self-healing ladder 'accreting + buggy' by the architecture audit (honor explicit fallbacks first, capability-aware bidding, backstops-as-removable-scaffolding still open) — memory project_architecture_audit_2026_06
Known flaky parallel test suite (pre-existing; validated by isolation + identical-FAIL-set-vs-HEAD) — memory project_swarm_philosophy_hardening
Autonomous bidding window is only 125ms in-process (swarm/bidding.ts:8) — effectively a local-bus formality rather than genuine market-based routing

Numerous eval-pending default-off flags (quorumEarlySynthesis, subAgentDisagreementVerify, clampSubAgentTimeoutToParent, taskGraphFailureDisposition, normalizeDelegationToEnglish, discoveryPrefetch, qaDeliveryLoop, detectWriteChurnOverwrite, crossAgentArtifactReuse, userProfilePrefetch...) are enabled only in this deployment's shard; recommending any of these as 'new work' would duplicate existing implementations — config/gateway/40-orchestration.jsonc vs packages/core/src/config/schemas/orchestration.ts defaults

Most restored honesty guards are schema-default OFF pending the user's pass^k live eval (citationHonestyGuard, urlFetchEnforcement, failedResearchHonestyBackstop, ungroundedFactualAnswerGuard, inlineArtifactFabricationGuard, subAgentPreEvidenceResearchForce, evidenceAnchoringOnGatheredEvidence, honestSynthesisOnPartialEvidence, freshnessHonestyGuard — config/schemas/orchestration.ts:60-120 all .default(false)); only four are enabled in the live shard per docs/honesty-restoration-2026-07.md, so a fresh install ships with the anti-fabrication net largely disarmed.

docs/honesty-restoration-2026-07.md:68-74 (explicit 'still open'): 6 live honesty guards still scope on deliverable-intent.ts's bilingual keyword fields — a latent de-lexicalization time-bomb; plus un-implemented tightenings: citation floor for short fabricated summaries, turn-scoped-vs-session evidence tightening, anchor length-scaling (exists in evidence-anchoring.ts:96 but opt-in only).

QA gates fail OPEN by design: parseQaVerdict treats unparseable/empty verdicts as PASS and the qaDeliveryLoop 'never blocks delivery' (qa-delivery-loop.ts:32-40) — a noisy/weak local reviewer model means bad answers ship with passed=true semantics; riskGatedQA only runs on plan-bearing turns, so a turn that never recorded a plan silently skips both QA gates (turn-plan.ts:174 comment documents this exact regression).

Evidence anchoring is lexical-overlap heuristics (token sets + spec-token regex, evidence-anchoring.ts), not semantic verification: a fluent wrong answer that reuses evidence vocabulary passes; the mutually-negated-token check covers only explicit negation contexts; stopword lists are EN+DE only.

Bilingual (DE/EN) assumptions are baked into honesty caveats (answerLooksGerman, citation-honesty.ts:44-48), memory stopwords, and shared-facts search stopwords — third languages get English defaults and diluted relevance scoring.

Warden thresholds are hard-coded module constants (warden.ts:49-113 — not config-tunable), and all counters are in-memory rolling windows that reset on gateway restart; no persistence or cross-instance aggregation.

engram document RAG /search is GLOBAL per instance with client-side post-filtering by source token (engram.ts:10-16) — scoping is enforceable only in our client, and the whole subsystem degrades SILENTLY to no-RAG when engram is down; deployment is pinned to the maintainer's homelab (10.10.0.2) per the setup-overhaul findings, so document RAG is effectively maintainer-only until Tier0 setup fixes land.

Graph memory requires MemGraph and degrades silently to flat-file (graph-service.ts:5-7); pgvector store likewise returns null/false silently — callers can't distinguish 'no results' from 'backend down', so retrieval quality regressions are invisible without checking logs.

Evals are real-LLM-traffic and stack-dependent: scene-eval/agent-eval assertions are brittle substring expectIncludes/Excludes; pass^k gating requires the user's local model stack (multiple shipped flags — qaDeliveryLoop rounds, staged-orchestration S3/S4, progressVerifierSemantic — are still 'live-eval pending'); the parallel vitest suite is pre-existing-flaky (validate by isolation).

Forced-synthesis abnormal-finish paths are corrected by a prepended caveat banner (prependTurnIncompleteCaveat), not by re-verification — the incomplete content still ships beneath the banner, and the banner dedup relies on sentinel phrase matching.

Shared session memory truncates aggressively (FACT_VALUE_MAX 2000 chars, RESULT_CONTENT_MAX 1200, RESULTS_MAX 50, 4h TTL) and the no-Redis fallback is process-local — cross-process/cross-instance sharing silently disappears; sub-agents also don't receive tagged skills (documented follow-up from the v0.13 wave).

Output Guardian is regex secret-scanning only (guardrails/output.ts SECRET_PATTERNS); the high-entropy detector is disabled for false positives — 'suspicious output' in the semantic sense is handled by the separate structural honesty guards, not this layer.

Turn scorecard/turn_performance events are emitted at severity 'warn' unconditionally (runtime.ts:4233-4251), muddying severity-based alerting; turn_scorecard is emitted from 6 different sites in runtime.ts, so field consistency across exit paths depends on manual duplication.

Known token-cost gap: B37 lean tool-catalog (the improvement-roadmap's biggest token lever) is NOT implemented — prompt trimming/compaction exists but the full tool catalog still rides every turn; roadmap items in docs/improvement-roadmap-2026-06.md §A-B are analysis-only.

researchDigest.area: Coordination/orchestration patterns in production LLM agent frameworks (2025-2026): what topologies won, what teams abandoned
patterns: Orchestrator-worker with codified effort-scaling heuristics (Anthropic Research system) [production-proven]
Single-writer, multi-reader (Cognition, Apr 2026) — parallel-writer swarms abandoned [production-proven]
Zero-shared-context review loop (coder → fresh-context reviewer on diff only → coder synthesizes) [production-proven]
Supervisor-first, graduate-to-swarm handoffs (LangGraph langgraph-supervisor / langgraph-swarm, Command-based handoff tools) [production-proven]
Handoffs vs agents-as-tools as distinct primitives with a decision rule (OpenAI Agents SDK) [production-proven]
Dual-ledger orchestrator with stall-triggered replanning (Magentic-One → Microsoft Agent Framework 1.0 'Magentic' orchestration) [production-proven]
Deterministic workflow agents wrapping LLM delegation (Google ADK: Sequential/Parallel/Loop agents + Coordinator/Dispatcher + shared session.state) [production-proven]
Cross-frontier 'Smart Friend' consultation — small-to-large difficulty escalation abandoned [emerging]

researchDigest.area: Context engineering & agent memory in 2025-2026: compaction, sub-agent isolation, agentic memory systems, scratchpads, KV-cache-aware design, JIT retrieval
patterns: Server-side context editing (tool-result clearing) + file-based memory tool [production-proven]
KV-cache-aware, append-only context layout (stable prefix; mask, don't remove) [production-proven]
Sub-agent context isolation with distilled returns + shared artifact store (orchestrator-worker) [production-proven]
Structured note-taking / scratchpad outside the window + recitation (todo.md pattern) [production-proven]
Self-editing memory blocks + sleep-time compute (Letta/MemGPT lineage) [emerging]
Write-time fact extraction pipeline vs temporal knowledge graph as the long-term memory layer (Mem0 vs Zep/Graphiti) [production-proven]
Just-in-time retrieval via lightweight identifiers instead of always-on context injection (grounded in context-rot evidence) [production-proven]
ACE — Agentic Context Engineering: evolving playbooks via incremental delta updates (no full rewrites) [emerging]

researchDigest.area: Reliability & anti-hallucination architecture for agent systems 2025-2026
patterns: Tiered verification stack (deterministic scanners → small fine-tuned judge → frontier LLM judge on sampled traffic) [production-proven]
Dedicated CitationAgent + end-state rubric judge (Anthropic multi-agent research system) [production-proven]
Small specialized groundedness/faithfulness models as an output rail (Vectara HHEM-2.x, Patronus Lynx, AWS Bedrock contextual grounding check) [production-proven]
Self-consistency majority voting over multi-agent debate (debate ≈ expensive sampling) [production-proven]
Externally-grounded reflexion only: self-correction loops must close on a deterministic oracle (compiler, tests, runtime probe), never on self-critique [production-proven]
Decompose-then-verify claim pipelines (Claimify / SAFE / VeriScore lineage; CoVe descendant) [emerging]
Diverse-family judge panels (PoLL) with correlated-error hygiene [emerging]
Uncertainty-gated abstention via semantic entropy / consistency scoring (LM-Polygraph, semantic-entropy probes, conformal variants) [emerging]

researchDigest.area: Model routing, cost/effort tiering, and budget allocation for LLM multi-agent systems (2025-2026 practice)
patterns: RouteLLM preference-trained binary router (strong-vs-weak win-probability routing) [production-proven]
Calibrated-confidence cascade routing (UCCI: cheap-first, escalate on calibrated error probability) [emerging]
Response-level draft-verify proxy (RLM-Cascade: speculative decoding at whole-response granularity) [emerging]
Speculative cascades (token-level cascade with flexible deferral rule) [research-only]
Token-budget-aware reasoning prompts (TALE: estimate-then-budget) [emerging]
Certainty-probe early exit (Certaindex / Dynasor probe-in-the-middle) [emerging]
Utility-curve budget allocation across pipeline phases (ZEBRA water-filling) [research-only]
Prompt-embedded effort-scaling rules + token-first budgeting (Anthropic orchestrator-worker practice) [production-proven]

researchDigest.area: Evaluating and observing agent systems (2025-2026): trajectory evals, pass^k reliability, LLM/agent-as-judge harnesses, online evals from production traces, OTel GenAI conventions, failure taxonomies and attribution
patterns: pass^k reliability metric + dual-control simulated-user harness (tau-bench / tau2-bench) [production-proven]
MAST failure taxonomy + automated LLM-judge failure annotator [emerging]
Automated failure attribution — Who&When (which agent, which step) [research-only]
OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions for agents (invoke_agent / execute_tool / chat spans) [production-proven]
Trajectory (trace-level) evaluation: full-trace judge scorers + per-step tool-call matching [production-proven]
Agent-as-a-Judge: evaluator with tool access that verifies intermediate states [emerging]
Online evaluation on sampled production traces (ingest-time filter -> async judge queue -> scores on traces) [production-proven]
Eval-gated CI: regression evals that block the merge (Braintrust-style) [production-proven]

researchDigest.area: Emerging agent architectures 2025-2026 (code mode, MCP scaling patterns, A2A, sandboxed runtimes, durable execution, best-of-N juries, plan-then-execute)
patterns: Code Mode / code-execution-as-tool-use (a.k.a. Programmatic Tool Calling) [production-proven]
Tool Search / progressive tool disclosure over large catalogs [production-proven]
A2A protocol (Linux Foundation Agent2Agent) with Agent Cards as the federation lingua franca [production-proven]
MicroVM agent sandboxes with snapshot-restore (Firecracker/Kata; E2B/Daytona/Modal-class runtimes) [production-proven]
Durable execution for long-horizon agents: super-step checkpointing + thread_id resume (LangGraph-style) vs replay-based durability (Temporal/DBOS) [production-proven]
Best-of-N with multi-agent aspect verifiers (BoN-MAV) / verifier juries, incl. multi-sequence verifiers [emerging]
Secure plan-then-execute with an explicit re-planner node (control-flow integrity against prompt injection) [emerging]
